output.brief: The rejects come from the combination of Arnholt resin and Press 5's degraded dryer (D5). Arnholt arrives wetter (0.27–0.33% at the dryer inlet). The healthy dryer D7 dries it to 0.07%, but D5 leaves it at 0.25–0.31%, above the 0.20% limit. Arnholt on Press 5 rejects about 10%. Arnholt on Press 7 rejects 0.8%. Quillan on Press 5 rejects 0.9%. Arnholt dried in a good portable dryer and run on Press 5 rejects 0.8%. The new operators are not the cause: first shift and second shift reject at the same rate on Press 5, and new and experienced operators match. Second shift only looks worse because all its VX runs on Press 5. Don't discipline the operators, and don't drop Arnholt. Do this week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore its original alarm limit, and verify the dew point is back to −40. Until then, keep Arnholt off D5 by sending it to Press 7 or a verified dryer. Add a moisture check at the press feed throat for every resin lot. Open question: Arnholt's wetter inlet resin may come from north-annex storage rather than the supplier, because every Arnholt sample came from that annex. Check this before paying for storage changes.
